name: Ignite
label: Revelation
lede: Ignite formed in Orange County and found its first big crowds in Germany. Along the way came a U2 cover its label vetoed, a singer who spent almost three years in Pennywise, and a replacement who auditioned by singing over two Ignite instrumentals.

eras.title: Three names before Ignite
eras.text: Bassist Brett Rasmussen and guitarist Joe D. Foster burned through Fuse, Angerslave and Shade first. The debut came out with two singers on it, and Zoli Téglás, the man who would define the band, showed up after it was recorded.

years.h: Ignite is the fourth name Brett Rasmussen's band tries
years.p: Rasmussen and guitarist Joe D. Foster had already been through Fuse, Angerslave and Shade. Joe Nelson and [[Gavin Oglesby|55402ba0-2241-4a42-9270-386964a84a79]] join, and [[Casey Jones|2a3fce86-361f-4deb-aefa-c711654de661]] plays drums.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Rasmussen and Foster first started playing together in 1992. Ignite's first demo carried five songs: Ash Return, Distance, Slow, Should Have Known and Far Away.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ignite (band) · Wikipedia: Scarred for Life
yt: Orange County, February 1994, with Randy Johnson
years.h: Scarred for Life has two singers, and neither is Zoli Téglás
years.p: Recorded at Moonsong Studios in Riverside, California, with Randy Johnson on tracks 1 to 5 and Joe Nelson on 6 to 8, over Brett Rasmussen, Joe D. Foster and Casey Jones. Lost & Found puts it out.
years.xp: Filmed a few months earlier, a February 28, 1994 Orange County set shows the band with Johnson at the mic, before Téglás arrived.

years.src: Wikipedia: Zoltán Téglás · Daily News Hungary
years.h: Zoli Téglás takes the mic and holds it for 27 years
years.p: California-born, the son of Hungarian immigrants, Téglás is recruited once Scarred for Life is finished.
years.xp:
Téglás was born on November 10, 1969. His father came to the US after World War II and his mother in the 1960s, and he grew up speaking Hungarian and spending childhood summers in Veresegyház, outside Budapest.

His own Wikipedia entry dates his arrival in Ignite to 1993; the band's entry says he came in after Scarred for Life was recorded.

eras.title: Germany gets there first
eras.text: A label dispute at home sent Ignite to Europe, where a Berlin label released their records and German crowds took to the band. Revelation Records brought them to America for an EP and a split, and then the original line-up came apart.

years.h: Téglás's first record with Ignite is Family
years.p: Ten songs made at For the Record St. in Orange County with producer Jim Monroe, released in Europe by Lost & Found.
years.xp: The same year brought the In My Time EP. With a label dispute in the way, Ignite went to Berlin's Conversion Records, which issued Call on My Brothers in America, built from the European material.

years.h: Revelation's first Ignite release is a split with Good Riddance
years.p: REV 53 is a 7". Revelation's own pressing notes say some of the 2,000 black vinyl first pressing came out with the two bands' labels switched.

years.src: Wikipedia: Past Our Means · Revelation Records: pressing history
years.h: Revelation releases the Past Our Means EP
years.p: REV 54 runs six songs in 14 minutes, recorded April 22 to 26 at Paramount Studios. The closer, Taken Away, has Téglás writing about Hungary.
years.xp: Produced by Jim Goodwin and the band. Revelation pressed 2,840 on black and 323 on blue the first time around, and has kept it in print since, most recently remastered in 2016.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ignite (band) · San Diego Punk: Brett Rasmussen interview
years.h: Japan, then Europe with Millencolin and Madball
years.p: German magazine VISIONS names Ignite the third best live band of 1996.
years.xp: Berlin's Conversion Records had been putting Ignite's records out since the label dispute at home, and German crowds made the band a live draw. Rasmussen later told San Diego Punk that "Berlin, London and Budapest are always really great cities for Ignite to play."

years.h: Casey Jones quits without warning, and Joe D. Foster follows
years.p: Scott Golley fills in on drums until [[Craig Anderson|08c50d56-7783-4411-bd94-36ffd87e11e7]] takes the stool for good. Brian Balchack takes co-founder Foster's place on guitar.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates Jones's exit to April 1997, in the middle of the Wonderland Festival Tour.

eras.title: The cover TVT wouldn't allow
eras.text: Ignite's breakthrough came on New York's TVT with A Place Called Home, with songs about veterans and poverty in English and Hungarian. Between tours Téglás did stunt work until a film injury hurt his spine. The U2 cover TVT vetoed finally came out six years later.

years.h: A Jackie Chan film leaves Téglás with a serious spinal injury
years.p: Between tours the singer works as a stunt performer. Wikipedia gives the date only as the late 1990s.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Place Called Home · Punknews: Ignite, A Place Called Home · San Diego Punk: Brett Rasmussen interview
years.h: A Place Called Home brings Ignite to a New York label
years.p: Thirteen tracks on TVT Records, including Veteran and Who Sold Out Now, plus the title track sung in Hungarian.
years.xp:
Producer Cameron Webb began with the band on pre-production in 1999 and stayed for the next two decades; the album itself credits Thom Wilson and Téglás as producers. Rasmussen told San Diego Punk: "We started working with Cameron Webb in 1999 with the pre-production of 'A Place Called Home'."

A Punknews reviewer called it "one of the most unique hardcore acts I've heard in a long time." Europe got the album in February 2001, timed to Ignite's run on the Vans Club Tour.

years.h: Revelation presses Call on My Brothers as a 12-inch
years.p: REV 91 starts with 538 copies on opaque purple. Revelation keeps re-pressing Ignite's 1995 Conversion album through 2016.

years.h: Ignite's singer takes the mic for the Misfits
years.p: Téglás sings North American dates with the Misfits and starts his side project, Zoli Band, the same year.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the tour to October and November 2000, after Michale Graves left the Misfits.

years.h: Nik Hill joins on guitar, and Ignite ride the Persistence Tour
years.p: Ignite play the European Persistence Tour package. Hill later starts Nations Afire with Brett Rasmussen and [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]]'s Chris Chasse.

years.h: A Troubadour DVD gets shot and never comes out
years.p: Ignite film a live DVD at the Troubadour in West Hollywood with A Dying Dream and Eightyonedays. Technical problems keep it off the shelves for good.

years.h: Abacus, Century Media's punk imprint, signs Ignite
years.p: The deal puts the band back in the album business after five years.

years.cap: Zoli Téglás at Rio Rock, April 2008
years.h: Six years late, Ignite's U2 cover makes it onto an album
years.p: TVT had vetoed Ignite's version of U2's Sunday Bloody Sunday for A Place Called Home. It closes Our Darkest Days on Abacus instead, produced by Cameron Webb.
years.xp:
The album takes aim at the Iraq war and the Bush administration, with songs like Poverty for All and Know Your History. A hidden track in Hungarian sits at the end of the last song.

The video for Bleeding, directed by Christopher Sims, came out on July 12, 2006. Nik Hill left that year to start Lucky Scars.

eras.title: Fronting Pennywise
eras.text: Ignite headlined the Persistence Tour, then lost their singer to a bigger band. Téglás fronted Pennywise for almost three years, until his back gave out on a German stage and Ignite went quiet.

years.cap: Ignite on the main stage at Resurrection Fest, Spain, August 2009
years.h: Ignite top the bill on the Persistence Tour
years.p: Six years after playing the package, the band headlines it, and spends the summer on festival main stages, including Resurrection Fest in Spain.

years.cap: Pennywise at Valley View Casino Center, San Diego, December 11, 2011, with Téglás as singer
years.src: Dying Scene: Zoli Teglas on Pennywise and Ignite · Wikipedia: Ignite (band)
years.h: Pennywise's new singer is Ignite's Zoli Téglás
years.p: He replaces Jim Lindberg on February 16. Ignite stay together and tour when they can while Téglás juggles Pennywise, Ignite and a solo album.
years.xp: Dying Scene's report said Ignite would carry on with Téglás, that Pennywise was already writing a new album from scratch, and that a solo album was due within days. Its author doubted the schedule: "I have no idea how the hell all of that is possible considering all the touring with Pennywise."

years.src: Loudwire: Zoli Teglas undergoes emergency surgery · Wikipedia: Zoltán Téglás
years.h: Téglás drops to his knees at With Full Force
years.p: A herniated disc stops Pennywise's singer mid-set at Germany's With Full Force festival. Loudwire reported doctors warned of possible paralysis; he had emergency back surgery on June 30.
years.xp:
Pennywise cancelled the rest of that European leg. Téglás's only Pennywise album, All or Nothing, came out in 2012, and he left the band that October; Jim Lindberg later returned.

Asked about making another record with Pennywise, Téglás quipped: "I don't know if there is going to be a next time because we might kill each other in the process."

years.h: Three years of part-time touring end in a full hiatus
years.p: Ignite had worked around Téglás's Pennywise schedule since 2010. In 2013 they stop altogether.

eras.title: Twenty-two years to a chart entry
eras.text: Ignite came back with Téglás and made their first album in a decade, and it charted in Germany and Hungary. Téglás moved into his grandmother's house outside Budapest, then walked away from the band in 2019.

years.cap: Ignite in front of an Our Darkest Days banner at Reload Festival, 2015
years.src: San Diego Punk: Brett Rasmussen interview
years.h: Ignite are back, and Téglás is full time again
years.p: The band starts its fifth album, again with Cameron Webb in the producer's chair.
years.xp: Rasmussen has called Webb "a very important part of Ignite."

years.h: A War Against You is Ignite's first chart entry anywhere
years.p: It reaches No. 12 in Germany and No. 5 in Hungary on Century Media, 22 years into the band.
years.xp: The album came out in January 2016 and was the band's first in a decade.

years.cap: Zoli Téglás at Impericon Festival, Oberhausen, April 2017
years.h: Two nights at Barba Negra, and a Hungarian flag on Téglás's arm
years.p: In Budapest on January 28 and 29, Téglás gets the Hungarian flag with the 1956 hole cut in it tattooed, with the words Never forget.
years.xp:
He told Daily News Hungary the idea came after a visit to Budapest's House of Terror museum, when a taxi driver asked him why he dwelled on the past. By then he'd inherited his grandmother's house in Veresegyház and moved in.

He also said hardcore barely exists in the USA anymore, with not many people to play for.

years.cap: Zoli Téglás at Full Force festival, June 2019, in his last year with Ignite
years.h: After 27 years, Zoli Téglás tells Ignite he's done
years.p: He says he will spend his time rescuing animals and on film and music projects, and plays the California dates already booked for early 2020.
years.xp: Téglás founded the Pelican Rescue Team, which picks up injured seabirds on the California coast and drives them to rehab centers, and volunteers as music and outreach coordinator for the Sea Shepherd Conservation Society. He also turns up in Terminator: Dark Fate (2019).

eras.title: A new singer with range
eras.text: Ignite didn't fold. Rasmussen went looking for a singer who could hit the notes, Holy Grail guitarist Eli Santana asked to try out, and the band made its first album in six years.

years.big: "I had so much fun hearing my voice on two of my favorite Ignite songs."
years.src: In Effect Hardcore: Who the F*ck Is Eli Santana · Wikipedia: Ignite (band)
years.h: Rasmussen wants metal guys who can hit the notes, and Anderson knows one
years.p: Eli Santana, on singing over two Our Darkest Days instrumentals drummer Craig Anderson sent him. Anderson had been asked by Brett Rasmussen for singers with range, and Santana, of Holy Grail, asked to try out.
years.xp: Santana sang Poverty For All and Bleeding, then auditioned on new material. The band introduced him with the Anti-Complicity Anthem EP and video, which also carried Turn XXI.

years.src: In Effect Hardcore: Who the F*ck Is Eli Santana
years.h: Santana's first Ignite show is Punk in the Park, with NOFX on the bill
years.p: He debuts in Silverado, California, in front of thousands, on a bill with [[Strung Out|0220a594-56a1-47ca-8288-001ead3a3546]] and [[NOFX|dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4]].
years.xp: Santana told In Effect he had one thought once the band got on stage: "Oh hell yeah, I love this shit!"

years.src: In Effect Hardcore: Who the F*ck Is Eli Santana
yt: Superbowl of Hardcore 2025, full set with Eli Santana
years.h: Ignite's self-titled album is the first with Santana
years.p: Nine new songs on Century Media, produced by Cameron Webb, the band's first album in six years.
years.xp: Santana said Webb "pushed me to deliver not only the right notes but also the right emotion."

yt: Sunday Bloody Sunday live, Hamden CT, September 2024
years.h: Thirty years in, Ignite hit the road with Slapshot again
years.p: East Coast dates with Slapshot, Death by Stereo and School Drugs, then a European run, again with Slapshot, to mark 30 years.

years.h: Téglás takes the pelican rescues to CBS Evening News
years.p: In May 2024 Ignite's former singer talks about the Pelican Rescue Team and its work on the California coast.
